cases.prompt: We call @Transactional placeOrder from inside the same service class and sometimes it runs without a transaction. Why?
expectations: Explains that self-invocation bypasses the Spring proxy so the annotation is inert
Moves the method to a second bean or uses TransactionTemplate for the explicit boundary
Adds a test that fails when the boundary is missing instead of relying on inspection

cases.prompt: GET /orders returns 200 rows in 900 ms and the log shows one select per row for the customer name. Fix it.
expectations: Identifies per-row lazy access on the customer association as the N plus 1 cause
Applies EntityGraph, join fetch, or a projection and states the cost of each
Sets open-in-view to false and adds a test that asserts the statement count for a realistic list size

cases.prompt: Page 800 of our report endpoint takes 9 seconds while page 1 takes 40 ms. The data set is 3 million rows.
expectations: Explains that offset pagination makes the database skip rows and that the cost grows with the offset
Moves to a keyset cursor with ScrollPosition and Window, or Slice when totals are not needed
Requires a stable total order with the primary key tiebreaker and non-nullable sort columns

cases.prompt: Two users editing the same order overwrite each other. We need a decision between optimistic and pessimistic locking.
expectations: Recommends @Version optimistic locking with a caller retry as the default
Justifies PESSIMISTIC_WRITE only for a database-enforced invariant such as stock decrement
Requires a concurrency test and notes lock ordering to avoid deadlocks for batch updates

cases.prompt: We need to archive 200k orders with a bulk update and the updated rows still show the old status in the same request.
expectations: Requires a transaction and clearAutomatically to evict stale entities from the persistence context
Sets audit columns inside the update statement because entity lifecycle listeners do not fire
Keeps the bulk update in bounded batches instead of one unbounded statement

cases.prompt: Our reporting endpoint joins six tables and aggregates. Should it stay on JPA repositories?
expectations: Recommends JdbcClient or jOOQ for the wide read-only join and keeps JPA for writes with invariants
Explains no proxy or N plus 1 cost in a hand-written query and the cost of losing compile-time query checks
Forbids mixing both for the same row set inside one transaction
